notesDetails.title: Why S3 & S6 Failed Holdout (5/7 vs. 7/7 Claimed): discard_exact/2 Double-Counted Partial recv Chunks, Breaking Live Chunked HTTPS (0/26) & Early-Returning Multi-Packet Bodies
bullets: Root Cause at `lib/capy_bench/http.ex:340` (`discard_exact/2` Recursion Bug): When streaming a fixed-length body or HTTP/1.1 chunk size across multiple socket reads, `discard_exact/2` receives `data` smaller than `remaining` and recurses with `discard_exact(%{conn | buffer: data}, remaining - byte_size(data))` instead of `%{conn | buffer: <<>>}`. Because `byte_size(data)` is simultaneously subtracted from `remaining` AND retained in `conn.buffer`, the next recursive frame counts those bytes a second time. The bug was written in Step 62 and survived Step 70's `binary_part/3` buffer-slicing patch untouched.

Live HTTPS & Multi-Packet Holdout Failures (S3 & S6): Against live `https://rizafahmi.com` (`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`), `discard_exact/2` terminates mid-chunk leaving body bytes in `conn.buffer`, causing `expect_crlf/1` to return `{:error, :invalid_response}` on every single request (`./cb https://rizafahmi.com` exited `1` with `Started: 26, HTTP responses: 0, Transport failures: 26`, whereas `./cb http://rizafahmi.com` passed with `49/49` HTTP `301` and `https://example.com` succeeded only because its tiny response fit in one TLS record). On a local multi-packet `Content-Length: 20` server sending `10` bytes, sleeping `500 ms`, then sending the final `10` bytes, `CapyBench.HTTP.get/2` returned `{:ok, 200, 21ms}` without reading the second half - violating both S3 (stream and discard complete body) and S6 (latency ends at body completion). Local tests missed the bug because `http_test.exs`'s chunked test sent tiny 5-byte chunks (`"hello"`, `" "`, `"world"`) in single TCP writes.

notesDetails.title: Clean Post-Boot S7 Ctrl-C via +Bi + SIGUSR2 (Boot-Window Exit 159 Race) & Unnoticed OTP TLS [notice] Pollution on stdout
bullets: All Post-Boot Foreground PTY Ctrl-C Probes Passed (S7 Verified): Unlike `omp-deepseek-v4-flash`'s `SIGTERM` `:erl_signal_handler` bug, `dsh` chose `emu_args: "+Bi"` with `cb` forwarding `INT` as `kill -s USR2 "$child"` into `System.trap_signal(:sigusr2, ...)` in `CapyBench.CLI.main/1`. Every post-boot foreground PTY probe exited `130` with a single valid partial summary on `stdout`, empty `stderr`, and intact `started == responses + failures`: `0.8s` pacing (`Started: 6, 200: 6`), `0.4s` and `0.8s` during a `1.5s` slow request (`Elapsed: 1.51-1.52s, Started: 1, 200: 1`), and `0.8s` and `1.2s` during a `3.5s` stalled request (`Elapsed: 2.00s, Started: 1, Transport failures: 1`).

Cold Boot-Window `Ctrl-C` Exit `159` Race & Step 99-103 Test Fixes: Because `cb` runs `"$here/cb_escript" "$@" &` without `( trap '' USR2; exec ... )` or a readiness handshake, sending `\x03` during the first `50-250ms` of cold BEAM startup kills `cb_escript` with default POSIX `SIGUSR2` disposition (`User defined signal 2: 31`, exit `159`, matching `omp-gemini-4-argon` and `agy-gemini-4-hydrogen`). The agent actually hit exit `159` at Step 99 when `ctrl_c_test.exs` sent `Ctrl-C` at `300-350ms`, and worked around it at Step 101 by bumping test delays to `900-1,000ms` (then fixed a Python-escaped `\\\\d` regex typo at Step 103).

False `PLAN.md` Claim on TLS Diagnostics (`stdout` vs. `stderr`): `PLAN.md` release verification claimed `"argument errors and TLS diagnostics were on stderr"`, but Step 112's own log shows `CapyBench.HTTP.tls_opts/1` omitted `log_level: :none`, causing OTP `:ssl` to dump `49` `[notice] TLS :client: ... generated CLIENT ALERT: Fatal - Unknown CA` blocks onto `stdout` ahead of `Target:` while `stderr` stayed empty.
